desc: Parse the input values $N, X$, arrays $A, B$, and permutations $P, Q$.
Construct two functional graphs: one where edges are $i \to P_i$ (for red balls) and one where edges are $i \to Q_i$ (for blue balls).

For each graph, compute the distance from every node $i$ to node $X$. Since $P$ and $Q$ are permutations, the graph consists of disjoint cycles with trees rooted on the cycles (edges directed towards the cycle). Actually, since it's a permutation, every node has out-degree 1 and in-degree 1. It is a collection of disjoint cycles.
Check reachability: For every box $i$ that contains a red ball ($A_i=1$), check if $X$ is reachable from $i$ by following $P$. If not, output -1. Same for blue balls ($B_i=1$) and $Q$.

If all balls can reach $X$, the minimum operations is the sum of the number of steps required for each ball to reach $X$? No. One operation on box $i$ clears $i$ and moves balls to $P_i$ and $Q_i$. We need to operate on $i$, then $P_i$, then $P_{P_i}$, etc., until we hit $X$. The set of boxes we must operate on is the union of the paths from all initial ball locations to $X$. Since $P$ and $Q$ are permutations, the path from any node to $X$ is unique. The set of required operations is the set of nodes $v$ such that there exists a ball starting at $u$ where $v$ is on the path from $u$ to $X$ in $P$ OR $v$ is on the path from $u$ to $X$ in $Q$.
Calculate the size of the union of these sets of nodes for both red and blue balls.
Write Python code implementing the cycle detection and set union logic.
Run the code against the provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
